Anything we propose should attach to one of those four, not sit beside them.

talking_points.why: His own pricing instinct, in his own numbers - quote against it, not over it.
talking_points.source_line: I'd rather go with a higher monthly fee because I don't want to rely on talent.

talking_points.point: The Boomtown decision is already made and it is a two-year one: stay on legacy Boomtown for the ad-buying power, migrate nothing, and build the replacement he owns. Pitching a migration is pitching against a decision.
talking_points.why: Agents tested Bold Trail and rejected it; moving 60 of them is impractical.

talking_points.point: On HomeCloneVault he already has money out the door and a partner circling - Origin Vault has asked him about a revenue-share partnership. That proposal is on HIS deal, not ours.
talking_points.why: Worth knowing before anyone proposes terms near it.
talking_points.source_line: Origin Vault. has asked me if I'll do some sort of a revenue share partnership.

talking_points.point: His own read on why a site converts is conversion science, not design taste - Boomtown gets him ~10% visitor-to-lead where he says some sites run 5%. Any site we hand him is judged against that number.
talking_points.why: It sets the acceptance criterion before we build.
talking_points.source_line: the site is only as good as it converts

benefits_to_us.benefit: The leak is quantified in his own numbers, not ours: ~$1,500/day on PPC, ~2 sales per 100 leads, ~$1,100 customer acquisition cost, and 85% of revenue on the one channel he says Google is closing. That is the whole leaky-bucket argument stated by the buyer.
He named the gap we close and admitted he cannot close it himself. Attribution reporting for organic is a deliverable, not a favour, and it is the one he will feel every week.
benefits_to_us.source_line: I don't know how to present that to them

benefits_to_us.benefit: He is already sold on the thesis. The work is not convincing him AI matters; it is being the one who ships before his October window.
benefits_to_us.source_line: I just feel like we have in our grasp institutional grade software

benefits_to_us.benefit: The SEO teardown was run live on his own site before any paperwork, and the schema defect is unfixable inside his hard-coded CMS template. That template constraint is precisely what a site we build removes.

He is paying an Upwork team on milestones for the internal app and calls it his first dev adventure. Four products, one first-time dev relationship and a hard October date is a delivery-capacity problem we are built for.
benefits_to_us.source_line: Built via Upwork dev team (milestone-based payments); first dev project undertaken
